name: Tennessee
nameStory: From Tanasi, a Cherokee town on the Little Tennessee River. What the word originally meant has been lost - the town is gone, and now sits under a reservoir. A state is named after a place nobody can visit and a word nobody can translate.
capitalStory: Nashville honors Francis Nash, a general killed at Germantown in 1777. Its position on the Cumberland River made it a trade hub, and the same rivers and rail lines that moved cotton later carried country music out of the hills and into the rest of America.

majorFeatures.name: Great Smoky Mountains
majorFeatures.note: Most visited national park in America

majorFeatures.name: Tennessee River
majorFeatures.note: Leaves the state, then comes back

funFacts: Tennessee touches eight states, tied with Missouri for the most.
The Tennessee River runs southwest into Alabama, changes its mind, and flows back north through Tennessee again to reach the Ohio.
The state constitution formally divides Tennessee into three 'Grand Divisions' - East, Middle, and West - and the three stars on the flag are those divisions.
The Smokies get their name from the natural haze the forest itself gives off.
whyItMatters: The Tennessee Valley Authority, created in 1933, dammed the river to control floods and generate power for one of the poorest regions in the country. It was the single largest experiment in the New Deal, and people still argue about whether the government should have done it.
